correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the general conductance-budget problem by homogeneity to L>=Pi, constructs X_s=Pi(I/2+(1-s)A_M/2)Pi, checks every edge quadratic form and computes its exact trace. Positive semidefiniteness holds sharply for s<=2 with at least two pairs and s<=2(n-1)/(n-2) with one pair. Exact primal weights attain the lower bound at both regimes and show gap one by a complete eigenspace basis. Strict dual definiteness below the price transition forces L=Pi and unique uniform conductances; strict marked-edge price slack above the transition forces zero on every marked edge. An extracted, local exact-rational program passed 35,388 assertions for all 4<=n<=18, every matching size; these finite tests supplement, not replace, the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed new statement is the complete two-price theorem for a matching in K_n, including the single-pair threshold 2(n-1)/(n-2), multi-pair threshold 2, uniqueness below the threshold and mandatory deletion above it. The inspected Sun et al. (2006) source provides general Laplacian semidefinite optimization and duality but not these exact pair-count-dependent formulas or rigidity; Boyd et al. (2007) uses discrete-time SLEM; Ghosh and Boyd (2006) treats upper bounds over graph families. Actual published-finding corpus searches for aliases and the K_n-minus-matching reduction returned no same spectral-gap price law. Residual specialist overlap is possible; absence of a retrieved match is not a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Specialist papers not identified by semantically ranked databases or keyword searches might already contain an equivalent two-price matching theorem.
The companion results cover other graph supports/objectives; no claim of global uniqueness of this topic is made.

value.rationale: An explicit, sharp price-screening law for network algebraic connectivity is a directly interpretable design result: a single costly link has a different critical price from two or more disjoint costly links, independent of n and matching cardinality in the latter case. It classifies optimizer rigidity below transition, unavoidable edge deletion above, and the precise optimal budget-to-gap tradeoff. These all-real-parameter, unrestricted-edge consequences are nontrivial beyond generic SDP or elementary graph eigenvalues and motivate the exact matching motif.
